derivations.claim: Setup and amplitude conditions. Since $\sin^2\alpha+\cos^2\alpha=1$, one has $|k_1|=|k_2|=K=\omega/c$ and $\hat k_1=\sin\alpha\,e_1+\cos\alpha\,e_3$, $\hat k_2=-\sin\alpha\,e_1+\cos\alpha\,e_3$; both $e_j^{\mathrm{amp}}$ are multiples of $e_2$, which is orthogonal to $e_1$ and $e_3$, so $k_j\cdot e_j^{\mathrm{amp}}=0$ by [F4], and with $b_j=k_j\times e_j^{\mathrm{amp}}/\omega$ the amplitude conditions of [F2] hold for both pairs; moreover $\delta(x)=(k_2-k_1)\cdot x=(-2K\sin\alpha\,e_1)\cdot x=-2K\sin\alpha\,x_1$, and $\hat k_1\cdot\hat k_2=-\sin^2\alpha+\cos^2\alpha=\cos2\alpha$ by [F4].

Clause (i). Apply [F1] with $a_1=a_2=1$ and the amplitudes $e_1^{\mathrm{amp}}=E_0e_2$, $e_2^{\mathrm{amp}}=E_0e^{i\varphi}e_2$: then $|e_j^{\mathrm{amp}}|^2=E_0^2$ and $e_1^{\mathrm{amp}}\cdot\overline{e_2^{\mathrm{amp}}}=E_0^2e^{-i\varphi}$, while $k_j\times e_2$ computed coordinatewise by [F5] gives $\hat k_1\times e_2=\sin\alpha\,e_3-\cos\alpha\,e_1$ and $\hat k_2\times e_2=-\sin\alpha\,e_3-\cos\alpha\,e_1$ (using $|k_j|=K$), hence $(\hat k_1\times e_1^{\mathrm{amp}})\cdot(\hat k_2\times\overline{e_2^{\mathrm{amp}}})=E_0^2e^{-i\varphi}(\cos^2\alpha-\sin^2\alpha)=E_0^2e^{-i\varphi}\cos2\alpha$ by [F4]; the bracket is therefore $E_0^2e^{-i\varphi}(1+\cos2\alpha)=2E_0^2\cos^2\alpha\,e^{-i\varphi}$, so $W=2E_0^2\cos^2\alpha\,e^{-i(\delta+\varphi)}$, $\operatorname{Re}(W)=2E_0^2\cos^2\alpha\cos(2K\sin\alpha\,x_1-\varphi)$, and $\langle u\rangle=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}(E_0^2+E_0^2)+\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\operatorname{Re}(W)=\varepsilon_0E_0^2[1+\cos^2\alpha\cos(2K\sin\alpha\,x_1-\varphi)]$ by [F1] and $\cos(-\delta-\varphi)=\cos(\delta+\varphi)$; this is clause (i).

Clause (ii). By step 2.1, at fixed $x_2,x_3$ the function $x_1\mapsto\langle u\rangle(x)$ is $\varepsilon_0E_0^2[1+\cos^2\alpha\cos(2K\sin\alpha\,x_1-\varphi)]$; since $\cos^2\alpha>0$ for $\alpha\in(0,\pi/2)$ and $\sin\alpha>0$, its oscillation has period $2\pi/(2K\sin\alpha)=\pi/(K\sin\alpha)=\lambda/(2\sin\alpha)$ with $\lambda=2\pi/K$, maximum $\varepsilon_0E_0^2(1+\cos^2\alpha)$ at $\cos(2K\sin\alpha x_1-\varphi)=1$ and minimum $\varepsilon_0E_0^2(1-\cos^2\alpha)$ at $\cos(2K\sin\alpha x_1-\varphi)=-1$; hence $V=\cos^2\alpha$, and $\cos^2\alpha=\frac12(1+\cos2\alpha)=\frac12(1+\hat k_1\cdot\hat k_2)$ by step 1.1. As $\alpha\downarrow0$ with $\alpha>0$ the value $\cos^2\alpha\to1$, and as $\alpha\to\pi/2$ it tends to $0$. At $\alpha=0$ one has $k_1=k_2$ and the profile is $\varepsilon_0E_0^2[1+\cos(-2K\sin\alpha\,x_1-\varphi)]$ evaluated at $\alpha=0$, which is the spatial constant $\varepsilon_0E_0^2[1+\cos\varphi]=2\varepsilon_0E_0^2\cos^2(\varphi/2)$: if this value is positive then max $=$ min and the displayed ratio is $0$, while if it vanishes (that is, $\varphi\equiv\pi\bmod 2\pi$) the ratio is the undefined expression $0/0$.

Clause (iii). If $k_1=k_2=:k$ with equal amplitudes and relative phase $\Delta$, then by [F1] (equal-wavevector clause) the sum is the single plane wave with amplitude $E_0(1+e^{i\Delta})e_2$, and $\langle u\rangle=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}|E_0(1+e^{i\Delta})e_2|^2=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}E_0^2|1+e^{i\Delta}|^2=\varepsilon_0E_0^2(1+\cos\Delta)=2\varepsilon_0E_0^2\cos^2(\Delta/2)$ using $|1+e^{i\Delta}|^2=2+2\cos\Delta$; scanning $\Delta$ over $\mathbb R$ gives maximum $2\varepsilon_0E_0^2$ at $\Delta\equiv0$ and minimum $0$ at $\Delta\equiv\pi$ modulo $2\pi$, so the phase-scan visibility $({\max-\min})/({\max+\min})$ equals $1$, a different quantity from the spatial visibility at fixed phase.

Clause (iv) and conclusion. Clause (i) is step 2.1, clause (ii) is step 3.1 and clause (iii) is step 3.2; clause (iv) records that all quantities above are deterministic field quantities of the stated ideal coherent preparation, that a measured fringe pattern or histogram would require a declared detector response, finite bin width, background, integration time and sampling model together with a statistical analysis, and that no observation or finite-sample visibility estimate is reported; in particular classical electromagnetic waves interfere, so the deterministic prediction alone does not discriminate between classical and quantum descriptions of light.
